cases.expected: Scope creation succeeds regardless of whether loadCollectors() has been invoked beforehand
cases.description: Create a CollectorContext, optionally call loadCollectors() (or skip it), then call enterDynamicScope(). The method should still create a dynamic scope without depending on collector loading.

cases.expected: A non‑null Scope instance is returned and CollectorContext.getDynamicScope() reflects this new scope
cases.description: Invoke enterDynamicScope() with no arguments and verify that the returned Scope object is not null and becomes the current dynamic scope of the CollectorContext.

cases.expected: A non‑null Scope instance is returned, identical in behaviour to the no‑arg overload
cases.description: Call the overloaded enterDynamicScope(null) and assert that it creates a Scope just like the default method (no‑arg) and that the current dynamic scope is set accordingly.

cases.expected: A non‑null Scope instance is returned that records the supplied JsonSchema
cases.description: Pass a mock JsonSchema object to enterDynamicScope(JsonSchema) and verify that the returned Scope is not null and that the scope internally references the provided schema (e.g., via a getContainingSchema() accessor if available).

cases.expected: Two distinct Scope objects are created; the second scope’s parent (or previous) is the first scope
cases.description: Invoke enterDynamicScope() twice in succession. Verify that each call returns a distinct Scope instance and that the second scope is linked to the first (e.g., via a getParent() method or by checking that getDynamicScope() after the second call returns the second scope while the first is still reachable as its predecessor).

cases.expected: Calling exitDynamicScope() after two enters returns the first entered Scope
cases.description: Enter two dynamic scopes, then call exitDynamicScope(). The method should return the Scope that was active before the most recent enter (i.e., the first Scope). After exit, CollectorContext.getDynamicScope() should point to that first Scope.

cases.expected: IllegalStateException (or a similar runtime exception) is thrown
cases.description: Create a fresh CollectorContext and directly invoke exitDynamicScope() without any prior enterDynamicScope() call. The method is expected to signal improper state by throwing an exception.

cases.expected: After exiting all entered scopes, CollectorContext.getDynamicScope() returns null
cases.description: Enter a dynamic scope, exit it, then call exitDynamicScope() again. The second exit should either throw an exception or leave the dynamic scope as null; the test asserts that the current dynamic scope is null after all scopes have been closed.

Pass a JsonSchema instance that is already linked to a different CollectorContext (simulated via reflection or a stub that reports an existing association). The method should reject re‑using the same schema in another context and throw IllegalArgumentException.

group: Enter When Internal Collector Map Is Null

cases.description: Create a CollectorContext, force its internal collector map (or similar required field) to null using reflection, then invoke enterDynamicScope(). The method is expected to attempt to access the map and consequently throw a NullPointerException.

group: Enter After Context Has Been Marked As Finished

cases.description: Assume CollectorContext provides a way to mark the context as finished (e.g., a hypothetical close() or freeze() method). After invoking that method, call enterDynamicScope(). The method should detect the illegal state and throw IllegalStateException.
